guard: the delivery daemon hosts the space's checkpoint timer writer on its scoped cred: a parked .schedule is armed and broker-fired with no manual pump, a poison request is terminated not redelivered, and the grant rows that authorize the pump are load-bearing
why: THE GAP WAS FOUND LIVE (lane F, 2026-09-02): nothing in production pumped the checkpoint timer
plane. The suites pump armCheckpointTimer by hand, and run-command.ts documented the delivery
daemon as pumping it, but the daemon had no such code and core's timerWriterGrants had zero
consumers — so no workflow pause on a live mesh ever expired. The build is three pieces, each
with a mutant aimed at it: the daemon's hosting loop (M1), core's pump (M2, M3), and the
delivery credential's new grant rows (M4, M5).
EVERY MUTANT'S COMMAND REBUILDS THROUGH THE SUITE SCRIPT: the daemon child runs `bin/cotal.ts`
via tsx, which resolves workspace packages to their compiled dist, so a source mutant is
invisible until built — the suite script's own `pnpm --filter cotal-ai... build` prefix is what
makes the mutation reach the process under test. The tool's restore verifies source, not dist;
after a proof, rebuild once by hand so the dist matches the restored source.

mutations.name: the daemon dials a connection but never starts the writer
mutations.replace: const handle: TimerWriterHandle = { stop: async () => undefined, done: new Promise(() => undefined) };
mutations.expectRed: the daemon's timer writer armed the parked .schedule (no manual pump ran)
mutations.cell: the daemon's timer writer armed the parked .schedule (no manual pump ran)
mutations.note: The hosting call replaced by an inert handle: the daemon logs nothing wrong and stays up, and only the pump is gone. Measured 2026-09-02 before this entry was written: the arm cell reds first, then everything downstream of it (target header, fire, poison drain); 6 passed, 6 failed.

mutations.name: the pump acks every request without arming anything
mutations.find: await armCheckpointTimer(ctx, { subject: m.subject, ...(m.headers !== undefined ? { headers: m.headers } : {}), data: m.data });
mutations.expectRed: the daemon's timer writer armed the parked .schedule (no manual pump ran)
mutations.cell: the daemon's timer writer armed the parked .schedule (no manual pump ran)
mutations.note: The pump consumes and acknowledges but the fenced arm never runs — the request plane drains cleanly while the space silently stops expiring pauses, which is exactly the shipped gap this build closes. Measured 2026-09-02: the arm cell reds first; the poison cells stay green because a swallowed request still drains; 7 passed, 5 failed. The 'writer logged the permanent refusal' cell also reds, so the split's log line is graded too.

mutations.name: a permanent refusal is naked instead of terminated
mutations.expectRed: the poison request is terminated: the writer's durable drains it and holds nothing pending
mutations.cell: the poison request is terminated: the writer's durable drains it and holds nothing pending
mutations.note: The ack-decision split inverted: a poison request that answers identically on every redelivery is retried forever. Measured 2026-09-02: exactly ONE cell reds — the poison-drain cell, because the naked message never leaves the consumer's pending state — and 11 pass, which is why the split needs its own mutant rather than riding the arm cell.

mutations.name: the delivery cred loses the timer-writer consumer rows
mutations.expectRed: the daemon's timer writer armed the parked .schedule (no manual pump ran)
mutations.cell: the daemon's timer writer armed the parked .schedule (no manual pump ran)
mutations.note: The shared grant set the pump binds with, removed at its one delivery consumer. The writer's bind is broker-denied, the supervised loop retries loudly, and nothing ever arms. Measured 2026-09-02: the arm cell reds first and the 'timer writer up' cell reds with it; 5 passed, 7 failed. Kills the row-set half of the permission story.

mutations.cell: the daemon's timer writer armed the parked .schedule (no manual pump ran)
mutations.note: The one publish this feature adds, removed alone: the writer binds and consumes fine but its authoritative .armed publish is broker-denied, so the arm fails as transient and retries forever.
